Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <537vql$9...@tron.sci.fi>, Marko Saari <gu...@sci.fi> wrote:

>1. Can I play Rötschreck against Pulled Fangs?

I'd say yes; as far as I know, however, the Rules Team's agin it.
A Tom Wylie ruling says the big R must be played when strikes are
declared, thereby disallowing its use at the time it's legal to
pull a fang.

>2. Can I play multiple Pulled Fangs at the same time (causing more
> aggravated damage) ?

Not as far as I know; once the first one resolves (as soon as it's played),
your target's in torpor and there is no opportunity to play another.

>3. Do I get manouver from Bum`s Rush if targeted minion blocks it?

Nope; BR offers the choice of remaining untapped or tapping to deny the
maneuver -- assuming the Rusher has no stealth, mind.

>4. according official tournament rules. IV Special Floor Rules. 1. Repeat
> actions rule: minions action is blocked and she untaps. Can she perform
> same action again in the same round?

This is still awaiting Shawn's pleasure -- where *is* that smooth
talking Irishman?

>5. Can I use damage preventation cards outside of combat? ie. Can vampire
> prevent damage from Carnas the Imp with Skin of Rock (or with Flak
> Jacket)?

Nay not, barring specific card errata, such as Rutor's Hand at superior.

>> maneuver -- assuming the Rusher has no stealth, mind.

>Does this mean that whenever I enter combat with someone who isn't
>choosing to block (Bum's Rush, Haven Uncovered, etc) they remain
>untapped after combat? Are they only tapped as a result of blocking?

Yes - only two things will tap a minion, outside of card text explicitly
stating that a minion is to be tapped. Those two things are:

acting (attempting an action)
blocking (successfully blocking an action)

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Pheersum <phee...@sb.net> writes:
>> L. Scott Johnson (sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu) wrote:
>>
>> : Yes - only two things will tap a minion, outside of card text explicitly
>> : stating that a minion is to be tapped. Those two things are:
>>
>> : acting (attempting an action)
>> : blocking (successfully blocking an action)

>This returns to a question I posted that has probably been answered

>before. If blocking, not combat taps the vamp, then if my opponent says,
>"Why yes, I won't block that Bum's Rush (Haven Uncovered, etc.) does
>that mean they remain untapped after combat?

That's exactly what that means. If you don't act and don't block, then
you don't tap. Explicit card text may allow other tap effects/options,
but this is the default behavoir.

Combat never results in a tap. Some cards (Brujah Frenzy) will cause
a combat and a tapping effects, and almost all blocks (which are tapping
effects) will cause combat, but combat itself doesn't tap anything.

decide which you want more in that case.
